rules.name: Project defines no tests
rules.short_description: The project has models but no detected tests in YAML or the test directory.
rules.long_description:
A successful dbt build runs the selected resources; it does not merely parse SQL. Without data tests, it cannot check undeclared assumptions about keys, relationships, or business results. This rule finds models with no detected YAML tests or test files. Tests managed outside this scan need a documented coverage contract.

## References

- [About dbt build command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/build)
- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [Overview of constraints](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constraints-overview)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
rules.remediation: Start with models used in joins and aggregations. Confirm the columns that define one row, check for duplicate key combinations, and check every primary-key column for nulls. Add a primary-key test only after both checks pass. Built-in unique and not_null tests are valid; this estate prefers dbt_constraints.primary_key when table constraint metadata is needed. Add relationship and business-rule tests next. Run dbt build with the intended selection so the tests execute with the models. Standard Snowflake PK/FK/UNIQUE metadata does not replace those tests.

references.title: Add data tests to your DAG

examples.title: Models with no tests
examples.bad:
models:
  - name: dim_customers
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
examples.good:
models:
  - name: dim_customers
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        tests:
          - dbt_constraints.primary_key

rules.name: Model has no primary-key or unique-key test
rules.short_description: No recognized primary-key or unique-key test covers the model; staging findings have lower priority.
rules.long_description:
A unique-key test checks whether a candidate row key repeats. A primary key must also contain no nulls. These checks can expose duplicate rows that would multiply a join result, but a passing key test does not prove all joins or business logic correct. This rule looks at column-level and model-level key tests. Staging findings are lower priority under the local policy.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
rules.remediation: Confirm the intended row grain before choosing a key. Check the candidate columns for duplicate combinations and check each column for nulls. Do not infer uniqueness from a name such as customer_id. If both checks pass and the key matches the business definition, add dbt_constraints.primary_key or equivalent unique and not_null tests. Define composite keys once at model level with column_names. Determine other columns' roles separately; they are not automatically foreign keys. Use arguments: for test inputs on dbt Core 1.10.5 and later; older versions use the legacy syntax shown in some examples. Check the installed engine and package version.

rules.name: Dimension has no dbt_constraints primary-key test
rules.short_description: A dim_* model lacks the estate-preferred primary-key test, even if unique and not_null tests exist.
rules.long_description:
This rule checks the local preference for dbt_constraints.primary_key on dimension models. Built-in unique and not_null tests already validate those data properties. The package can also create primary-key metadata on supported table models; it does not create constraints on view or ephemeral models. Standard Snowflake tables do not enforce PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, or UNIQUE constraints. RELY metadata requires accurate, regularly tested data.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [Overview of constraints](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constraints-overview)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
rules.remediation: Confirm the dimension's grain and current test coverage. For a supported table model, use dbt_constraints.primary_key if the estate requires primary-key metadata. Review package settings and permissions before enabling constraint creation. Keep built-in tests when they satisfy the contract and document the policy exception; do not assume that a missing package-specific test means the data is untested.

rules.name: Fact table has untested key-shaped columns
rules.short_description: A fct_* or fact_* model has _id columns without recognized foreign-key or primary-key coverage.
rules.long_description:
A foreign-key test checks whether non-null values have a matching referenced key. Without that check, an inner join can discard unmatched fact rows. The _id suffix is only a hint: confirm the column's actual role and the referenced table. Add a separate not_null test if null foreign keys are invalid.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
- [Overview of constraints](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constraints-overview)
rules.remediation: Identify the referenced model and validate its primary or unique key. Add dbt_constraints.foreign_key or a relationships test for each confirmed relationship. For package tests, set pk_table_name and pk_column_name to the verified parent key; use the corresponding multi-column arguments for composite relationships. If unknown members are allowed, agree on their treatment with the owner. A sentinel such as -1 works only if a matching dimension row exists and that meaning is intentional. Use arguments: for test inputs on dbt Core 1.10.5 and later; older versions use the legacy syntax shown in some examples. Check the installed engine and package version.

rules.name: Built-in tests can use dbt_constraints equivalents
rules.short_description: A unique/not_null pair or relationships test can use a package-specific test under the estate policy.
rules.long_description:
This is a package-style recommendation, not evidence that the built-in tests are inadequate. dbt_constraints offers primary_key, unique_key, and foreign_key tests, including composite-key forms. It can also generate constraints from supported built-in tests when enabled, so replacing a test is not always necessary to get metadata. Constraint creation depends on materialization, settings, privileges, and test results. Snowflake standard-table PK/FK/UNIQUE constraints are not enforced.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
- [Overview of constraints](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constraints-overview)
rules.remediation: Check the package version and generated metadata before replacing working tests. If the estate requires the explicit form, replace unique plus not_null with dbt_constraints.primary_key, or relationships with dbt_constraints.foreign_key. Preserve the original arguments, null policy, filters, and severity when they remain appropriate. Review any change that enables RELY; keep tests running after data changes. Use arguments: for test inputs on dbt Core 1.10.5 and later; older versions use the legacy syntax shown in some examples. Check the installed engine and package version.

      field: customer_id
examples.good:

  - dbt_constraints.foreign_key:
      pk_table_name: ref('dim_customers')
      pk_column_name: customer_id

rules.name: Key-test coverage is below the local threshold
rules.short_description: Fewer than 60% of models have a key test; this rule excludes projects with fewer than five models.
rules.long_description:
This rule measures how many models have a recognized key test. The default 60% threshold and five-model minimum are local policy, not dbt requirements. Coverage is a count of detected tests, not proof that tests ran or that the data is correct. Missing key tests leave assumptions about row grain unchecked.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
rules.remediation: Start with consumer-facing dimensions and facts, then review upstream models. Confirm each model's grain before adding primary-key or unique-key tests. Add foreign-key tests for verified relationships. If the project has no tests, follow SSC-EWI-DBTTST0001 first, then use this finding to track coverage. Document models that intentionally have no unique grain rather than inventing a key to meet the threshold.

rules.name: Singular test may be reusable as a generic test
rules.short_description: A single-table null or count assertion without joins may fit a reusable generic test.
rules.long_description:
A singular data test is a SQL query for a specific assertion. A generic test is a parameterized query that can be attached to multiple resources in YAML. This rule identifies simple single-table null/count checks without joins as candidates. It does not prove that a built-in test has identical behavior.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
rules.remediation: Compare the assertion with a built-in generic test such as not_null, unique, or accepted_values. Use the generic form only if it preserves the result and configuration. For reusable custom logic, define a test block under tests/generic or macros and attach it in model YAML. Keep a singular test when its business logic is specific or a generic form would obscure it.

rules.name: Test failure storage is not enabled
rules.short_description: No enabling store_failures setting was found under data_tests or tests in dbt_project.yml.
rules.long_description:
store_failures saves failing records for later inspection, up to the configured limit. Without it, test results still report failures and the compiled query can be rerun. Stored results replace the previous results for that test; they are not an append-only history. This rule checks project-level configuration, so a command-line flag or test-specific setting can provide coverage elsewhere.

## References

- [store_failures](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/store_failures)
- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
rules.remediation: If retained failing rows are appropriate, set +store_failures: true under data_tests in dbt_project.yml and choose an approved schema. Confirm create/access permissions and review which sensitive columns the test selects. Limit access and retention as required by the data policy. Use test-specific settings when broad storage is unnecessary. Remember that subsequent runs replace the stored failures.

rules.name: Snapshot configuration is incomplete
rules.short_description: A SQL snapshot lacks unique_key or strategy, or the timestamp/check strategy lacks its required field.
rules.long_description:
Snapshots use a unique key and a change-detection strategy. The timestamp strategy needs updated_at; the check strategy needs check_cols. Missing settings can cause validation or compilation failures. This rule scans SQL snapshot blocks and does not establish the complete inherited configuration. It does not prove that history was silently lost.

## References

- [Add snapshots to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/snapshots)
rules.remediation: Check the snapshot's effective configuration first, including inherited settings in dbt_project.yml. Add missing values at the appropriate level. Use timestamp when the source has a reliable modification timestamp; otherwise select the check columns deliberately. Validate key uniqueness and run the snapshot in a safe environment. Newer dbt versions also support YAML snapshot definitions; check version-specific syntax instead of copying a legacy SQL block blindly.

rules.name: Model and YAML property entry do not match
rules.short_description: A model has no detected YAML property entry, or a YAML entry has no detected model.
rules.long_description:
Model property files hold descriptions, column metadata, and generic data tests. A missing entry leaves those properties undeclared in the scanned files, but the model can still have singular tests or SQL-level configuration. An entry without a matching model may be stale or outside the scan's discovered resources; verify before deleting it. Missing model entries are grouped by folder, with names in context.models.

## References

- [Model properties](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/model-properties)
- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
rules.remediation: Add property entries for the listed models in a YAML file under the configured model paths. Include useful descriptions and tests that match each model's grain. For an entry without a model, check enabled state, model versions, discovery scope, and recent renames. Correct the name or remove the entry only after confirming it is obsolete.

rules.name: Key-shaped column has no recognized key test
rules.short_description: A model with an existing key test has another key-shaped column without recognized key coverage.
rules.long_description:
A key-shaped name is a candidate for review, not proof of a primary or foreign key. This rule checks uncovered columns only when the model already has a key test. Model-level composite keys count as coverage for their listed columns. TST0002 owns models with no key tests; TST0004 handles fact-model key coverage.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [dbt Constraints package](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/dbt_constraints)
rules.remediation: Check each column's meaning and data. Use a foreign-key test only for a verified relationship to another model. Use a unique-key test for a separate unique value, and a primary-key test only for the model's row grain with no nulls. Define composite keys once at model level. Do not create a foreign key back to the same entity merely because its name resembles the model. Document columns whose naming convention does not denote a key. Use arguments: for test inputs on dbt Core 1.10.5 and later; older versions use the legacy syntax shown in some examples. Check the installed engine and package version.
